newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end up, shrug off Sakakibara comments.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end up, shrug off Sakakibara comments.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo trade higher on Friday, ignoring comments by a senior Finance Ministry official who termed the JGB market "bubbly".
June JGB futures closed up 0.23 at 126.85, after trading in a narrow range between 126.70 and 126.94.
Turnover of the benchmark contract was 37,714.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, told Reuters in an interview that the JGB market was considerably "bubbly" and he saw a risk of the bubble bursting.

Sakakibara also said it would be dangerous for financial markets to assume that Japan will not raise interest rates within the next year. He said it would be natural for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates when it has confirmed the economy's strength.
The interview came out during Tokyo's midday break. Following Sakakibara's remarks, June briefly fell as low as 126.50 on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX).
Traders said some foreign players sold JGB futures on SIMEX, but Japanese players reacted calmly.
Despite recent bullish comments about the economy by government officials, most players do not expect a near-term credit tightening by the BOJ, traders said.
Some city banks were detected buying cash JGBs at the long-end of the yield curve, traders said.
Also, the 3.0 percent 20-year JGB issued in April attracted investor bids after its yield rose to par on Thursday.

"We are starting to see bids in corporate bonds, which had fallen quite a bit recently. Dealers' positions are becoming lighter compared with earlier in the week," a trader at another brokerage house said.
Next week, market participants will be focusing on a 10-year JGB auction and the BOJ's branch managers' meeting.
Traders said the new 10-year JGB's coupon is likely to be set at either 2.3 or 2.4 percent.
"If June JGB futures rise above 127.00, the coupon is likely to set at 2.3 percent. Whichever it is, the new JGB should meet good investor demand," the second trader said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.155 percent as of 4.22 p.m. (0722 GMT), down from 2.175 percent on Thursday.
